title: South Korea at the World Cup
description: From 2002 semi-finalists to 2022 giant-killers — how well do you know South Korea's World Cup history?

questions.q: South Korea co-hosted the 2002 World Cup with Japan. What was their extraordinary result?
questions.explain: South Korea reached the semi-finals of the 2002 World Cup as co-hosts, beating Poland, USA, Portugal (group stage), then Spain and Italy in the knockout rounds — the best ever result by an Asian nation.

questions.q: South Korea beat Italy in the 2002 round of 16 through a dramatic golden goal. Who scored it?
questions.explain: Ahn Jung-hwan headed the golden goal winner in extra time. Ironically, Ahn played for Italian club Perugia, whose president famously sacked him after the goal — calling it 'a deadly sin against Italian football'.

questions.q: How did South Korea beat Spain in the 2002 quarter-finals?
questions.explain: South Korea and Spain drew 0–0 after extra time, with South Korea winning 5–3 on penalties. Spain had two goals controversially ruled out for offside, adding to the drama.

questions.q: South Korea lost the 2002 semi-final to Germany. Who scored the only goal?
questions.explain: Michael Ballack scored in the 75th minute to give Germany a 1–0 win. South Korea then lost the third-place play-off 3–2 to Turkey, finishing fourth overall.

questions.q: At the 2022 World Cup, South Korea qualified for the round of 16 by beating which European nation in the group stage?
questions.explain: South Korea beat Portugal 2–1 in their final group game, with Hwang Hee-chan scoring a last-minute winner to send them into the knockout stage. They were eventually eliminated by Brazil 4–1.

questions.q: Which South Korean player — a long-serving captain — plays his club football for Tottenham Hotspur?
questions.explain: Son Heung-min has been South Korea's captain and talisman, as well as a Premier League star at Tottenham Hotspur where he has consistently finished among the league's top scorers.

questions.q: South Korea's first ever World Cup appearance was in 1954. What record did they hold for years after that tournament?
options: First Asian nation to score a WC goal
First Asian nation to reach the knockout rounds
Heaviest defeat in World Cup history
First WC hat-trick by an Asian player
questions.explain: South Korea suffered a 16–0 defeat to Hungary at the 1954 World Cup — at the time the heaviest defeat in World Cup history. Hungary also beat them 7–0 the same tournament.

questions.q: Park Ji-sung was South Korea's greatest player of his era. Which English club did he play for from 2005–2012?
questions.explain: Park Ji-sung played for Manchester United under Sir Alex Ferguson, winning four Premier League titles and a Champions League. He was a vital, tireless midfielder famous for his work rate.

questions.q: South Korea's national team is known by which nickname?
questions.explain: South Korea are known as the Red Devils (붉은 악마) — a reference to their red home kits and passionate support. The name gained global recognition during their 2002 home World Cup run.

questions.q: In which year did South Korea first qualify for the World Cup without co-hosting — confirming their status as a true football nation?
questions.explain: South Korea qualified for the 1986 World Cup in Mexico — their first qualification on merit (excluding 1954 where they were placed directly). They have qualified for every World Cup since, a record of consistency in Asian football.
